claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,n), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md with the negation map and the GLV endomorphism recovers x with probability at least 0.544 (hence at least 0.39) at the stated mean step budget, with expected total work at most 2^128.140687 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification, under the disclosed random-walk heuristic of proof.md Section 4. Peak memory is at most 2^102.62 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^15.0 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. This is an analytic argument, not a claim of practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the Pollard rho walk logic with negation-map and GLV quotient canonicalisation, distinguished points, cycle detection with restart, and collision resolution on a small additive cyclic group. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho with negation map and GLV endomorphism
